title: Available power calculation
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the power available for additional lamps as the difference between delivered power (generator output minus line loss) and factory consumption.

title: Number of lamps
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the number of additional light bulbs by dividing the available power by the rated power per bulb, yielding 2600.

title: Transmission line current
description: Important: The student must correctly determine the current in the high-voltage transmission line using the power loss formula I = sqrt(P_loss / R).

title: Step-up transformer ratio
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the transformer current ratio relationship (inversely proportional to turns) using generator output current and transmission line current, yielding 1/10.

title: Step-down transformer ratio
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the voltage at the step-down transformer input (accounting for line voltage drop) and apply the transformer voltage ratio to find the turns ratio, yielding 230/11.

title: Power conservation reasoning
description: Optional: The student explicitly states or uses the principle of power conservation for ideal transformers (input power equals output power) in their reasoning.

title: Ignoring line loss in lamp power
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly uses the generator's output power directly (200 kW) instead of the delivered power (184 kW) when calculating available power for lamps.

title: Incorrect transformer ratio direction
description: Pitfall: The student confuses the voltage/current ratio relationship for transformers, leading to an inverted turns ratio (e.g., 10/1 instead of 1/10).
